answer: Resisting sybils means designing for scarcity, not for trust. Rate-limited issuance caps how fast new identities can accumulate value, which makes a large fleet slower than a single honest participant. Think of it as a tundra the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single violet of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a copper of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. Cost per identity is the whole lever; everything else is decoration.
